Gastrointestinal endoscopy for dogs

Endoscopy lets us look inside the oesophagus, stomach and upper intestine without open surgery, and take biopsies in the same session. In brachycephalic dogs it matters because chronic regurgitation is often a gastrointestinal problem sitting alongside the airway problem, not instead of it.

A hiatal hernia or a sliding oesophagus shows up on endoscopy and changes the anaesthetic plan for airway surgery. We regularly scope bulldogs before a soft palate procedure for exactly that reason, and the two findings together explain most cases of persistent regurgitation after surgery.

The procedure is done under general anaesthesia and takes thirty to sixty minutes. Dogs go home the same afternoon. Biopsy results take five to seven working days.
